answers: The industrial designer provided several options respectively for energy, material and interface. Among these options, the industrial designer preferred traditional battery, titanium and simple push buttons so that they would have enough money for speech recognition. After that, the user interface designer proposed an LCD display only for output, which might be taken into account. The group also talked about how to enable the users to find their controllers.

full.prediction: The discussion about industrial components focused on selecting materials and energy sources for the remote control. The team decided to use batteries instead of solar cells due to energy reliability concerns. They opted for titanium over rubber or plastic for its aesthetic appeal, despite manufacturing challenges with double-curved shapes. Push buttons were chosen over LCD displays to reduce costs and complexity, while also incorporating speech recognition technology to enhance functionality within budget constraints.
full.measured_scope: physical node KV storage; eager gather temporaries excluded, no latency claim
